required_behavior: Keep product promise, editions, ports and externally owned resources distinct.
unsafe_inference: A data product is its dataset, table, API or distribution.

required_behavior: Require scoped identity authority and explicit mappings.
unsafe_inference: Matching product names establish identity or equivalence.

required_behavior: Use explicit directional edition relations and compatibility evidence.
unsafe_inference: A larger version string proves replacement, compatibility or currentness.

required_behavior: Treat registration as a separate effect occurrence describing the product.
unsafe_inference: A catalog or registry record is the product edition.

required_behavior: Bind semantic role, exact contracts and provider locations separately.
unsafe_inference: A port is just a URL, table location, topic or credential.

required_behavior: Evaluate exact multidimensional readiness criteria and evidence.
unsafe_inference: A structurally closed port graph proves readiness.

required_behavior: Require externally issued scoped authority and accountability bindings.
unsafe_inference: Repository author, team proximity or on-call role implies product authority.

required_behavior: Keep self-assessment, external appraisal and certificate identities separate.
unsafe_inference: A product's readiness verdict is independent certification.

required_behavior: Retain independent evidence dimensions and applicable criteria.
unsafe_inference: One quality, FAIR or SLO score proves product readiness.

required_behavior: Require separate scoped approval and publication effect receipt.
unsafe_inference: Readiness automatically publishes a product.

required_behavior: Marketplace offer and ranking remain independently owned.
unsafe_inference: Publication creates a marketplace listing or endorsement.

required_behavior: Require policy, entitlement and fulfillment decisions from their owners.
unsafe_inference: Publication grants access or provisions data.

required_behavior: Limit the claim to the exact target registration effect.
unsafe_inference: Publication receipt proves consumers can discover or consume the product.

required_behavior: Track population, delivery, acknowledgement and migration separately.
unsafe_inference: A delivered notice proves every consumer understood and migrated.

required_behavior: Require explicit population definition, cuts and coverage evidence.
unsafe_inference: Usage logs are a complete subscriber/dependency census.

required_behavior: Keep deprecation, sunset, recall, revocation and deletion distinct.
unsafe_inference: Deprecation means behavior changed, access ended or the product was deleted.

required_behavior: Preserve history and issue explicit effects to owning contexts with receipts.
unsafe_inference: Recall deletes the product and all downstream copies.

required_behavior: Evaluate integrity, semantics, migration, provider independence and substitutability separately.
unsafe_inference: A complete checksum-valid exit package proves semantic portability.

required_behavior: Require closed dependencies, obligations, in-flight work, recalls and exit evidence.
unsafe_inference: An elapsed sunset or notice window proves safe decommission.

required_behavior: Allow attributed proposals only; named authorities and deterministic laws retain every consequential decision.
unsafe_inference: A model or agent may establish identity, waive readiness, approve publication, recall or decommission.
